curated_relationships.explanation: Same fact, different documents and phrasing: the deck's headline '740 Mn Express parcel shipments in FY24' matches the annual report's '740 million parcels for FY24'. The AR adds the FY23 base (663 million) and the exact growth rate (11.48%), which rounds to the deck's 11.5%.

Unit conversion: the deck reports EBITDA in ₹ crore (₹127 Cr) while the annual report reports ₹ million (₹1,266.41 Mn). ₹1,266.41 Mn = ₹126.64 Cr ≈ ₹127 Cr. The FY23 bases also agree: ₹(4,516.08) Mn = ₹(451.6) Cr ≈ deck's ₹(452) Cr. Same underlying fact, different units and rounding.

1.4 million tons (deck) ≈ 1,429 thousand tonnes (annual report) — the deck rounds to one decimal, the AR is exact. Growth rates agree: 29.8% (deck) vs 29.82% (AR), from the same FY23 base of 1,101K tonnes.

The deck's exact quarterly count (33,278 active customers in Q4 FY24) is consistent with the annual report's rounded 'over 33,000 active customers' as of March 31, 2024. Different precision, same underlying fact.
Deck segment chart shows Express Parcel revenue of ₹5,077 Cr in FY24; the AR states ₹50,765.87 million = ₹5,076.6 Cr ≈ ₹5,077 Cr. Chart rounding vs statutory disclosure of the same figure.

Both documents project CPI headline inflation for the SAME fiscal year (FY2025/26), yet the IMF (Article IV, Nov 2025) says 2.8% while the RBI (Annual Report, Aug 2025) says 4.0% — a 1.2 percentage point gap. This is a genuine conflict between two official projections. Context that partially explains it: the IMF report is later and incorporates the post-GST-reform disinflation and collapsing food prices, which the RBI's earlier report could not fully anticipate. The system flags this for human review rather than silently picking a winner.

Apparent conflict: the 2022 prospectus lists Suvir Suren Sujan as a sitting Non-Executive Nominee Director, while the FY24 annual report says he 'resigned from the Board with effect from August 24, 2023'. Reconciled by time: the prospectus speaks as of May 2022; the resignation took effect ~15 months later. Both documents are correct for their respective dates.

Same document, same year, two very different 'loss for FY24' figures (₹1,679.68 Mn vs ₹2,491.86 Mn). Reconciled by scope: the first is the STANDALONE loss, the second the CONSOLIDATED loss (which includes subsidiaries). The comparison must read the accounting basis, not just the number.

Both state CPI headline inflation for 'FY25' but over different windows: the Economic Survey (written Jan 2025) covers April–December 2024 (4.9%); the RBI Annual Report (Aug 2025) covers the full fiscal year 2024-25 (4.6%), which includes the sharp food-inflation decline in Q4 (Feb–Mar 2025) that the Survey could not yet observe. Different coverage windows, not conflicting data.

Deck says 'revenue from services ₹8,142 Cr'; AR says 'revenue from operations ₹81,415.38 Mn'. ₹8,142 Cr = ₹81,420 Mn ≈ ₹81,415.38 Mn (rounding). Two further wrinkles: the deck's figure EXCLUDES traded goods revenue while the AR's is total revenue from operations, and the units differ (crore vs million). Reconciled via unit conversion + scope note; the ~0.006% residual is rounding.

Naive chart reading gives 'PTL freight revenue ₹1,429 Cr' from the deck, but the AR's statutory figure is ₹15,174.05 Mn = ₹1,517.4 Cr — 5.8% apart with no honest reconciliation. The real story is an extraction failure: PDF text extraction separates chart numbers from their labels, and '1,429' is actually PTL TONNAGE in '000 tonnes (matching AR's 1,429K tonnes), not revenue. See the Failures section for the full post-mortem.

IMF projects 6.6% growth for FY2025/26 (Nov 2025); RBI projects 6.5% for 2025-26 (Aug 2025). Nearly identical — the 0.1pp gap reflects forecast vintage: the IMF incorporates the stronger 2025Q2 outturn (7.8%) and GST reform effects that post-date the RBI report.

The Economic Survey's FY26 growth range (6.3–6.8%, published Jan 2025) brackets the IMF's later point estimate (6.6%, Nov 2025). A range vs a point forecast from different vintages — consistent rather than conflicting.
RBI's 6.5% projection for 2025-26 sits inside the Economic Survey's 6.3–6.8% range for FY26. Different institutions, consistent outlooks.

failures.detail: Text-order jumbling in the earnings deck's segment charts (PDF pages 9-10): numbers are emitted in a different stream order than their chart labels, so label-adjacency extraction reads '1,579 / 1,101 / 1,429' next to 'PTL freight revenue' when those numbers are actually PTL TONNAGE in '000 tonnes; the real PTL revenue series is 1,705 / 1,157 / 1,517 (₹ Cr). Detected via cross-document check against the annual report (₹15,174.05 Mn = ₹1,517.4 Cr PTL revenue; 1,429K tonnes PTL volume). Mitigation in place: every fact's quote is verified against page text, and cross-doc numeric mismatches are surfaced as relationships for review. Planned improvement: layout-aware chart extraction (bbox clustering via pymupdf words) so numbers inherit the coordinates of their chart title/legend.

showcase.title: Corroborated across documents (different wording + units)
showcase.narrative: Deck headline 'EBITDA ₹127 Cr / 1.6%' vs annual report 'EBITDA ₹1,266.41 Mn'. Different units (crore vs million rupees), different precision — the system normalizes units (₹1,266.41 Mn = ₹126.6 Cr ≈ ₹127 Cr) and verifies both quotes against the source pages. Also see: express parcel shipments (deck '740 Mn' vs AR '740 million parcels, up 11.48%') and PTL tonnage (deck '1.4 Mn Tons' vs AR '1,429K tonnes').

showcase.title: Genuine contradiction: FY2025/26 CPI projection (IMF vs RBI)
showcase.narrative: Two official projections for the same period, same indicator: IMF 2.8% vs RBI 4.0% — a 1.2pp gap the system refuses to wave away. The explanation cites both quotes, notes the publication-order context (GST reform disinflation post-dates the RBI report), and marks the pair for human review instead of forcing agreement.

showcase.title: Apparent contradictions reconciled by context (time / scope / units / coverage)
showcase.narrative: Director example: prospectus (May 2022) lists Suvir Suren Sujan as a current director; annual report says he resigned effective Aug 24, 2023 — TIME reconciles them. Three more reconciliations in the dataset: standalone vs consolidated loss (SCOPE), Survey Apr–Dec CPI 4.9% vs RBI full-year 4.6% (COVERAGE WINDOW), and deck ₹8,142 Cr services revenue vs AR ₹81,415.38 Mn revenue from operations (UNITS + rounding + label scope).

showcase.title: Extraction failure found, handled, and documented
showcase.narrative: Naive label-adjacency extraction reads the deck's PTL chart as 'revenue ₹1,429 Cr in FY24' — wrong: PDF text order separates chart numbers from labels, and 1,429 is tonnage ('000 tonnes). The cross-document check against the AR's statutory ₹15,174.05 Mn (=₹1,517.4 Cr) exposed it. Handling: quote-verification on every fact, cross-doc mismatch surfacing, a Failures log in the API/UI, and a planned fix (bbox-based chart extraction). Every system that extracts from real PDFs has failures — this one surfaces its own.
